subject: Enable and disable UI elements in the "input" and "output" R objects

messages.author: 2f3428d3166aad1c
messages.subject: Enable and disable UI elements in the "input" and "output" R objects
parts:
From previous discussions, it seems that the easiest way of having having a dynamically defined number of inputs or outputs is done by choosing a reasonable maximum number of possible number of inputs/outputs and defining a numbered set inputs/outputs up to the maximum number, e.g.

MAX <- 200

lapply(seq_len(MAX), function(i) {
   output[['impl']]$defineOutput(
      paste("dynamicOutput_", i, sep=""),
      reactive(function() {
         paste("Dynamic input ", i, " will go here but it depends on input dummy=", input$dummy, sep="")
      })
   )
})

Then, based on some user input, the actual number of these elements that are used could be much smaller than MAX.  An example could be that I want a user input for each column of a data frame, where I don't know the number of columns of the data frame up front, and the number of columns will change throughout the application.  

Now suppose I want MAX to allow for the possibility of many inputs/outputs (hundreds), but the actual number will typically be quite small (< 10).  This number will be changed relatively infrequently in the application.

Further suppose that these dynamic UI elements also depend on some other input, which changes frequently.

Setting MAX to anything too large will cause updating to be very slow, even if only a few of the elements are actually being used.

I have a simple gist that illustrates this.  There is a numericInput that lets you choose the number of dynamic elements to show, and a dummy input on which all of these elements depend.  Setting MAX to be too large really bogs things down.

runGist("4383290")

What would be nice would be to have the ability such that when the definition of the number of dynamic elements to show is changed, to be able to disable elements in the "input" or "output" shiny R objects that will not be used.

Maybe there is an easier way around this?
